text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen nearly 2% over the past week, sliding further today as crude oil prices have climbed into the $107–$115 range amid escalating Middle East tensions and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. While rising oil prices typically benefit refiners by supporting fuel margins, the sharp climb driven by geopolitical risk rather than solid demand appears to be creating uncertainty — refineries are running near full capacity (93.4%), but gasoline and diesel inventories remain elevated, suggesting demand hasn't kept pace with the price surge.

The stock's weakness reflects a broader tension: geopolitical risk premiums baked into crude prices don't always translate to refiner profits if refined product demand doesn't follow. A refiner makes money on the *spread* between what it pays for crude and what it sells gasoline or diesel for — when oil jumps on fear rather than actual consumption, that spread can compress rather than expand.
